s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopic findings of segmental erythema and ulceration
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
No evidence of perforation, abscess, or diverticulosis
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopic findings of segmental erythema and ulceration
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
No evidence of perforation, abscess, or diverticulosis
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Ulcerative Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy, subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Crohn's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT, elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Infectious Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bloody diarrhea and elevated fecal calprotectin, despite negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays

shortlist.label: Microscopic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Normal colonoscopy appearance in some segments, with subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Ischemic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea, with mild thickening of the colon on CT

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon, with normal-appearing mucosa in other areas, is consistent with Crohn's Disease, which can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract in a skip lesion pattern. The presence of subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ulcerative Colitis
rejected.why: Typically involves the rectum and extends proximally in a continuous manner, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Infectious Colitis
rejected.why: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Microscopic Colitis
rejected.why: Characterized by normal endoscopic appearance, which is not consistent with the segmental erythema and ulceration seen in this patient

rejected.label: Ischemic Colitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with a history of low blood flow or vascular occlusion, which is not mentioned in the patient's history
